name: Local Assistant Development Capability
summary: The assistant can handle most course labs, general coding, workspace migration, database exercises, computer-network labs, partial self-upgrades, repeated local testing, and real-browser webpage reading, mainline ToyOS implementation with local runtimes and cheap workers, keeping premium-model use focused on architecture, theory gaps, data risk, security boundaries, and hard failures. It can also scan a new workspace, infer the local stack, and suggest a low-cost execution path before invoking premium models. It now also structures work as a software delivery pipeline with requirements, roles, rules, git workflow hints, and validation checkpoints.
capabilities: Read public or login-gated webpages through a real local Edge or Chrome process when browser automation is permitted
Capture page title, body text, links, and optional screenshots through the browser bridge
Read assignment prompts and restate exact requirements before editing
Inventory new local folders and migrate them into resources, project memory, and reusable task templates
Locate target files and produce minimal patches for xv6 and other course labs
Handle common multi-language coding tasks with small verified patches
Prepare SQL queries, migrations, and schema updates for MySQL- or openGauss-oriented tasks
Run computer-network labs with local socket, packet, and HTTP tools
Compile and build local projects in WSL
Run repeated QEMU smoke tests for OS kernels
Capture debug logs and compare pass/fail markers
Draft concise experiment reports and answer explanations from observed results
Approve at most one cheap post-failure probe before pausing
Apply low-risk self-upgrades to prompts, templates, test scripts, capability manifests, and UI text
Act as the main implementation worker for ToyOS under WSL and QEMU guardrails
Escalate only failed, ambiguous, or high-risk cases to the core planner
Generate local deployment starter files and release checklists before cloud credentials are available
Inspect local MySQL, openGauss, Docker, and SQL tooling before escalating database tasks
Read network keepalive logs and surface current proxy and queue state in the UI
Generate markdown lab reports with embedded local screenshots from observed experiment results
Derive structured task contracts with requirements, deliverables, constraints, acceptance criteria, and risks
Assign product, architect, coder, tester, reviewer, ops, and supervisor roles to a task
Evaluate basic rule-engine checks before execution and expose git workflow expectations
Run a cheap-first meta-factory maintenance loop and persist factory state plus self-upgrade candidates
Expose factory status so the user can drive the platform from a single control surface
Generate isolated systems into workspace/{project} from reusable system templates
Evaluate generated systems against template manifests and repair missing required paths
Use a bounded generator/evaluator/fixer loop as the Layer 3 core instead of free-form generation
Run automated AI reliability checks for context boundaries, false premises, instruction-following, uncertainty handling, and freshness awareness

execution_policy.database_runtime: MySQL CLI, local MySQL Server, or document-driven setup workflows when configured
execution_policy.network_runtime: curl, ping, ss, tcpdump, Wireshark-compatible captures, and WSL networking tools
execution_policy.migration_runtime: local folder inspection, resource registration, project memory, and reusable task templates
execution_policy.self_improvement_scope: low-risk local assets only; no autonomous security, permission, or packet-capture privilege changes
execution_policy.core_model_role: failure analysis, theory clarification, data-risk review, security review, and architecture decisions
execution_policy.browser_runtime: playwright-core bridge with local Edge or Chrome
